# Objetivos del archivo:

1. Remove any ASVs that are **cloroplasts**
2. Remove ASVs that are **mitochondria**
3. Check for **reverse complements**
4. Check los **sequencing depth** y decidir acerca
del acerca del minimo para rarefaccion
5. Finalizar el archivo physeq `preprocessed_physeq`

## Input
1. **Raw phyloseq object**: `data/02_AssignASVs/raw_phyloseq.RData`

## Output
1. A pre-processed phyloseq object (S4 object): `data/03_PreProcessing/preprocessed_phyloseq.RData`
# Load Data

```{r load-physeq}
# Load physeq
load("data/its/02_Assign_ASVs/raw_physeq.RData")

# Ver el formato
raw_physeq
```

# Clean up the data!

## Remover todo lo no_fungi
```{r rm-!fungi}
# Mantener estrictamente solo a los ASVs asignados al reino Fungi
fungi_physeq <-
  raw_physeq %>%
  subset_taxa(Kingdom == "k__Fungi")

# How many ASVs were non-fungi (e.g., host DNA, plants, protists)?
numNonFungi_ASVs <- ntaxa(raw_physeq) - ntaxa(fungi_physeq)

numNonFungi_ASVs

# Eliminar secuencias que no tienen asignacion a nivel de phylum 
clean_physeq <-
  fungi_physeq %>%
  subset_taxa(!is.na(Phylum))

# How many ambiguous ASVs were removed?
numAmbiguous_ASVs <- ntaxa(fungi_physeq) - ntaxa(clean_physeq)
numAmbiguous_ASVs
```

<span style="color: red;"> Pregunta 1: Que contaminantes buscaste y cuantos habian? El dataset tenia controles positivos o negativos? como se manejan los controles? </span> 
  
there is no controls nor mock communities so we can go ahead to Reverse complements

## Buscar complemento reverso
```{r reverse-complements}
# Pull out Taxa Table
tax_table <- 
  clean_physeq %>%
  tax_table() %>% 
  data.frame()

# Grab ASV Sequences and Names
asv_names <- tax_table$ASV
asv_seqs <- tax_table$ASVseqs

# Create empty comparison matrix
asv_rev_comp <- matrix(nrow=length(asv_seqs), ncol = length(asv_seqs)) 

# Fix the names in the rows and columns 
rownames(asv_rev_comp) <- asv_names
colnames(asv_rev_comp) <- asv_names

# Convert sequences to Biostrings
asv_dna <- DNAStringSet(asv_seqs) 

# Inspect 
head(asv_dna)

# Construct reverse complement
asv_rev_dna <- reverseComplement(asv_dna) 

# Now loop through every asv sequence to check 
for(i in 1:length(asv_seqs)){ # For each asv sequence...
  match_vec <- asv_dna[i] == asv_rev_dna # Compare it to the reverse complement of every other sequence...
  asv_rev_comp[,i] <- match_vec # Write that logical vector as a new column 
}

# Find how many TRUEs (matches) we have, divide by 2 because each pair occurs twice
cat("For", sum(asv_rev_comp) / 2,"ASVs, the reverse complement will need to be removed") 

# The current data objec
clean_physeq
```

# Asesorar la profundidad del resto de las muestras

```{r read-depth}
# El objeto actual
clean_physeq

# Make a metadata_df for joining
metadata_df <- 
  clean_physeq %>%
  sample_data() %>% 
  data.frame()

# What is the library size/sequencing depth for each sample? 
seqSums_df <- 
  clean_physeq %>%
  otu_table() %>%
  # Sum each sample column 
  colSums() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "sample_names") %>%
  left_join(., metadata_df, by = "sample_names")

# Rename second column 
colnames(seqSums_df)[2] <- "TotalSeqs"

# check
dim(seqSums_df)
head(seqSums_df)

# Show the depth of samples 
seqSums_df %>%
  dplyr::select(sample_names, TotalSeqs) %>%
  arrange(TotalSeqs) %>%
  head()

# plot it as a bar plot 
numSeq_bar_plot <-
seqSums_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=reorder(sample_names, TotalSeqs), y = TotalSeqs,
             fill = localidad)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = localidad_colors) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) + 
  labs(y = "Read Depth", x = "Sample")

# histogram
numSeq_hist_plot <- 
  seqSums_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= TotalSeqs, fill = localidad)) + 
  geom_histogram(color = "black") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = localidad_colors) +
  labs(y = "# of Samples", x = "Read Depth") + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Density plot 
numSeq_density_plot <-
seqSums_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(TotalSeqs, fill = localidad)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = localidad_colors) +
  labs(x = "Read Depth")


# Put it all together 
numSeq_bar_plot + numSeq_hist_plot + numSeq_density_plot + 
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") 

# What's the min seq depth? 
min(sample_sums(clean_physeq))

# Final check of the sequencing depth for now
seqSums_df %>%
  dplyr::select(sample_names, TotalSeqs) %>%
  arrange(TotalSeqs)
```

# Run iNEXT

```{r iNEXT-biodiversity}
# prepare the input data 
# Species in rows and the samples in columns 
iNEXT_input_df <- 
  clean_physeq %>%
  otu_table() %>%
  data.frame()

# Inpect 
dim(iNEXT_input_df)
iNEXT_input_df[1:5, 1:5]

# Run iNEXT 
# Remember to set the seed!
# ASVs in ROWs, samples in COLUMNS 
iNEXT_data <- iNEXT(iNEXT_input_df, 
                    q = c(0, 1, 2),
                    datatype = "abundance")
```

## `ggiNEXT` Rarefaction Curves 
```{r iNEXT-colors}
# Extraer metadata para los colores
iNEXT_color_df <- 
  clean_physeq %>%
  sample_data() %>%
  data.frame() %>%
  # Asegúrate de usar la variable correcta de tu diseño experimental (ej. 'localidad')
  dplyr::select(sample_names, localidad)

# arreglar los nombres con guiones 
inext_names <- gsub("-", ".", iNEXT_color_df$sample_names)

# Crear el vector de colores por muestra
colores_por_muestra <- localidad_colors[iNEXT_color_df$localidad]
names(colores_por_muestra) <- inext_names

# Extraer una muestra por localidad para tener una leyenda (ahora estamos asignando el color a cada muestra entonces si dibujamos una leyenda default va a tener cada una de las muestras)
localidades_unicas <- unique(iNEXT_color_df$localidad)
# Buscamos la primera muestra que coincida con cada localidad
muestras_representantes <- inext_names[match(localidades_unicas, iNEXT_color_df$localidad)]
```

## Plot main curve
```{r plot-iNEXT-rarefaction}
# Curvas de Rarefacción con ggiNEXT
ggiNEXT(iNEXT_data, type = 1, facet.var = "Order.q") + 
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold")) + 
  scale_color_manual(name = "Localidad",
                     values = colores_por_muestra, 
                     breaks = muestras_representantes, # Solo muestra 5 elementos en la leyenda
                     labels = localidades_unicas) +    # Renombra esos 5 elementos con las localidades
  scale_fill_manual(name = "Localidad",
                    values = colores_por_muestra, 
                    breaks = muestras_representantes, 
                    labels = localidades_unicas) +
  guides(shape = "none") + # elimina la leyenda de las formas de los nodos de la muestra
  labs(y = "Effective Number of ASVs", x = "Number of Sequences")
```

## Curve per localidad
```{r manual-rarefaction}
# 1. Preparar la metadata para el cruce (creando una columna puente con puntos)
meta_for_join <- metadata_df %>%
  mutate(names_inext = gsub("-", ".", sample_names))

# 2. Extraer los datos matemáticos de iNEXT y unirlos con tu metadata
iNEXT_manual_df <- 
  iNEXT_data$iNextEst$size_based %>%
  dplyr::rename(names_inext = Assemblage) %>%
  left_join(meta_for_join, by = "names_inext")

# 3. Dibujar las curvas separadas por localidad
iNEXT_manual_df %>%
  # Filtrar solo los datos interpolados reales (Rarefaction)
  dplyr::filter(Method == "Rarefaction") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = m, y = qD, color = localidad, group = sample_names)) + 
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.8) + 
  # Crear paneles: Filas = Números de Hill (q=0, 1, 2), Columnas = Localidad
  facet_grid(Order.q ~ localidad, scales = "free") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = localidad_colors) + 
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(y = "Effective Number of ASVs", x = "Number of Sequences") + 
  # Apagamos la leyenda porque los títulos de los paneles superiores ya indican la localidad
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        strip.text.x = element_text(size = 8, angle = 0))
```
